 Oral Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal by judgment dated 30.08.2016 passed in MVC No.240/2014 by Prl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Dharwad.

2. The case of the claimant in brief is as under:
On 07.02.2013 at about 11.30 p.m., the deceased Prasad Kolekar was proceeding as a pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-47/H-7518 from Hubli towards Dharwad side, the rider of the said motor cycle was riding the same in a rash and negligent manner, at that time the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-25/C- 2600 came from Dharwad towards Hubli in a rash and negligent manner and both the drivers have lost control over their respective vehicles and dashed to each other and caused accident.
Due to the accident the deceased Prasad fell down and sustained fatal injuries over the NC: 2024:KHC-D:13047 body.
After the accident Prasad was shifted to SDM, Hospital and while taking treatment deceased Prasad died in the said Hospital.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was working as a Electrician and earning Rs.15,000/- per month and he was contributing the same towards his family.
He was the only earning member in his family and entire family was depending upon him.

3. The appellant/claimant made a petition claiming compensation, the Tribunal after recording evidence, has awarded compensation as under:
Sl.No. Heads Rs.
1. Loss of Dependency Rs.6,48,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs.16,034/-
3. Loss of love and affection Rs.1,00,000/-
4. Loss of estate Rs.50,000/-
5. Transportation, Funeral and Rs.25,000/-
Hemavati W/O Vasant Kolakar vs Santosh S/O Ramanna Harapanahalli on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153346800/
2  obsequies  Total Rs.8,39,034/-
4.
The claimant not satisfied with the award of compensation by the Tribunal has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2/insurance company.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant would contend that the deceased was aged 21 years and he was an electrician and the Tribunal has taken income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month but it ought to have taken at Rs.7,000/- per month as per chart prepared by the legal services authority for the year 2013.
He contends that the Tribunal has not awarded future prospects.
With this, he prayed to allow the appeal.
7. The learned counsel for the respondent would contend that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
He contends that the compensation awarded for loss of love and affection, loss of estate and transportation of dead body and funeral expenses are on higher side.

With this, he prayed to dismiss the appeal.
8.
Having heard learned counsels, the Court has perused impugned judgment, award and the other materials placed on record.
It is not in dispute that the deceased was aged 21 years as on the date of death and the accident has taken place in the year 2013.

The Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/-
per month.

As per chart prepared for settlement of disputes in Lok-Adalat by legal service authority,
the notional income fixed for the year 2013 is Rs.7,000/-.
The Tribunal ought to have taken the said notional income.
The Tribunal has not awarded the future prospects.
As the deceased was aged 21 years, he is entitled to future prospects at 40%.

10. In view of the above, the appellant/claimant is entitled for loss of dependency is as under:
Rs.9800/-(7000+2800) x 12 x 18 x 50% = 10,58,400/-
11.
The claimant is mother of the deceased and deceased was a Bachelor and therefore, claimant is entitled to consortium in a sum of Rs.40,000/-.
Apart from that, the claimant is entitled to loss of estate in a sum of Rs.15,000/- as against Rs.50,000/- as awarded by the Tribunal.
The claimant is entitled to funeral expenses and NC: 2024:KHC-D:13047 transportation of dead body in a sum of Rs.15,000/- as against Rs.25,000/- as awarded by the Tribunal.

The claimant is not entitled to loss Hemavati W/O Vasant Kolakar vs Santosh S/O Ramanna Harapanahalli on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153346800/
3 of love and affection as awarded by the Tribunal in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- as consortium is awarded to the claimant.

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has rightly awarded medical expenses in a sum of Rs.16,034/-.
12.

In view of the above, the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation as under:
Sl.No. Heads Rs.
1. Loss of Dependency Rs.10,58,400/-
2.

Medical expenses Rs.16,034/-
3. Loss of consortium Rs.40,000/-
4. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
5. Transportation, Funeral and Rs.15,000/-
 obsequies
Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs,11,44,434/- as against Rs.8,39,034/- awarded by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has awarded interest at 8% p.a. on the compensation and it is on higher side and therefore, appellant/claimant is entitled NC:
2024:KHC-D:13047 to interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on enhanced compensation.

14. In view of the above, the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii. The appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.3,05,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.

iii. The respondent No.2/insurance company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment, failing which it is liable to pay interest at 9% p.a. Sd/-
